sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: OpenMontage is an open-source, agentic video production system. It turns an AI coding assistant like Claude Code or Cursor into a video studio: you describe a video in plain language and the agent researches, scripts, generates or finds footage, narrates, edits and renders it.
sixtySeconds.problem: Making even a short explainer or trailer takes research, scripting, assets, voiceover, music and editing across many tools. OpenMontage runs that whole pipeline from your coding assistant, and can work from free stock footage and open archives as well as paid AI video models.
whoFor: Creators making explainers, shorts and trailers
Developers who use Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Windsurf or Codex
Anyone wanting AI video without a closed platform
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a code-driven, transparent video pipeline that runs in the AI assistant you already use, with cost estimates before generation. Paid video and voice providers cost money per use.
requirements: Optional API keys for image, video, voice and music providers

overview: You open the project in your AI coding assistant and ask for a video, such as a 60-second animated explainer. The agent picks a pipeline, researches the topic with web search, writes and narrates the script, generates or finds images and footage, adds royalty-free music and word-level subtitles, and composes the result with Remotion.

It can also start from a reference video (a YouTube video, Short, Reel, TikTok or local clip), analyse its pacing and style, and propose two or three concepts with cost estimates and a sample before full production. A local board called Backlot shows the production live and pauses on a scene-by-scene contact sheet so you approve visuals before rendering.

All provider keys are optional; more keys unlock more tools. Supported providers include fal.ai (FLUX, Veo, Kling), Kling, ElevenLabs, OpenAI, Google, Suno and free stock sources like Pexels, Pixabay and Unsplash.

troubleshooting.problem: npm install fails on Windows with ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE
Certificate or pip errors in an existing environment
troubleshooting.solution: Upgrade with python -m pip install --upgrade 'pip>=26.2.2' 'certifi>=2026.10.19' and restart Python processes.
